zones.name: Northwest Zone
zones.html:
NW Zone -

  • Fall Chinook fishing has been slow in the North Coast rivers. The Trask and Wilson Rivers remain the biggest producers but harvest has dropped off even in those basins. Rain predicted over the weekend might bring in a few more fresh Chinook but the season is winding down. In addition beginning Dec 1 all North Coast Rivers and bays close to angling for Chinook. Fishing has really slowed down in the bays with very few fish being harvested.
  • The Trask River and North Fork Nehalem River have hatchery coho salmon runs and a few fish are being caught though, overall, fishing has been slow. Hopefully the rains predicted for Thanksgiving will bring in some fresh fish.
  • Hebo Lake and Town Lake were stocked with trophy trout a couple weeks ago. This was an unscheduled stocking. These are big trout that are fun to catch!
  • Fall Chinook fishing has been slow in the Siletz, Alsea, Siuslaw, Yaquina and Salmon rivers. As a reminder, Chinook are spawning in many systems and anglers are asked to be mindful of fish on redds. Refer to Fall Coastal Salmon Management for more information on season outlines and bag limits. Siltcoos and Tahkenitch lakes are open for wild coho retention. Anglers are having some success in Siltcoos Lake, and more fish should push in with the large tides and expected rain.
  • The Port of Newport public fishing pier will be closed until at least Monday Nov. 30 for safety reasons.

zones.name: Southwest Zone
zones.html:
SW Zone –

  • Rogue-South Coast Wild Steelhead season runs Dec. 1 - Apr. 30. During this season, a Rogue-South Coast Steelhead Validation is required to fish for wild steelhead in the Rogue Basin and South Coast. Anglers who want the opportunity to keep wild winter steelhead must also purchase the Rogue-South Coast Steelhead Harvest Tag.
  • Empire, Saunders, and Butterfield Lakes were stocked recently with legal trout. Bradley Lake and Powers ponds were stocked the week of Nov 15.
  • Diamond Lake is still producing some nice rainbows, along with catch and release brown and tiger trout. The forecast has some cold wet weather for the weekend.
  • Recent rains have kick started fall chinook fishing in the Elk and Sixes Rivers. As always anglers will want to watch the weather and try to fish as river flows are dropping after a rain event. This is a good time of year to visit Elk River Hatchery with fall chinook returning to the hatchery on a daily basis.

Rogue Basin Waterbodies

AGATE LAKE: bass, carp, crappie, yellow perch, brown bullhead

Agate Lake is 14 percent full, and the boat ramp is likely not usable by trailered boats. Bass, panfish, and carp are available. Anglers are encouraged to target carp especially when they are concentrated during the drawn-down portion of the year. Last updated 11/24/26.

APPLEGATE RESERVOIR: trout, landlocked spring chinook, largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, black crappie, bluegill

Trout fishing should be good especially near the head of the reservoir where reports of very good catches along Carberry Cr have come in recently. Applegate's surface elevation is 1,872 feet, and boat access is limited to the low water boat ramp at French Gulch. The water surface temperature is 50F. Check up-to-date reservoir levels here, or call the Army Corps of Engineers at 800-472-2434 for flow and temperature information. There is a longstanding health advisory for consumption of resident species due to elevated levels of mercury. See Oregon Health Authority consumption guidelines or the sportfishing regulations for more information. Last updated 11/24/26.

APPLEGATE RIVER below Applegate Dam: trout

The Applegate is very low and clear right now. Try using small presentations and be stealthy approaching the bank to avoid spooking fish. Concentrate on surface chop areas or deeper pools with structure. Only adipose fin clipped rainbow trout may be retained. All wild rainbow and cutthroat trout must be released unharmed. Consult the fishing regulations for more information. Last updated 11/24/26

EMIGRANT LAKE: largemouth and smallmouth bass, black crappie, bluegill, brown bullhead, catfish, rainbow trout

Emigrant is currently 15 percent full and launching small boats may still be possible. Anglers can still enjoy fishing from inflatables or other small watercraft, or fishing from shore. Just be prepared for a muddy shoreline. There is a longstanding health advisory for consumption of resident warmwater species in Emigrant for high levels of mercury. Consult the sportfishing regulations or the Oregon Health Authority for more information on consumption guidelines. The most current elevations for Emigrant Reservoir and other Rogue Basin reservoirs can be found on the Bureau of Reclamation's website, here. Last updated 11/24/26.

EXPO POND: rainbow trout, largemouth bass, bluegill, black crappie

Bass and panfish are available and might be an easy Thanksgiving/Free Fishing Weekend outing. Try rubber baits like senkos or brush hogs on a jig and let them dead drop for bass in cool conditions. Expo Pond is the pond at the Jackson County Fairgrounds located directly adjacent to the access road at Gate 5, at the Southern Oregon RV Park.

There are Chinese mystery snails in the most northern pond. They are highly invasive and were illegally dumped here. Please do not move these creatures and drain and dry any personal watercraft before using them in another waterbody. Last updated 11/24/26.

FISH LAKE: rainbow trout, brook trout, spring Chinook

Fish Lake is slowly filling and is 32 percent full and ice-free. The USFS boat ramp is not available, but the Fish Lake Lodge ramp may still be usable for some boats. Fall fishing can be very good for rainbow trout. Anglers are encouraged to report catches of tiger trout or any other fish stories to Rogue Fish District Staff 541-826-8774. Last updated 11/24/26.

HOWARD PRAIRIE: trout, largemouth bass

Howard Prairie is 45 percent full and the county ramps are closed for the season. Small boats may be able to launch near the dam. Several anglers have reported high catch rates in recent weeks as the temperatures are cool and trout are widely distributed. Anglers are reminded to remove all vegetation from gear, boots and boats before leaving Howard Prairie. Last updated 11/24/26.

HYATT LAKE: trout, largemouth bass

Hyatt is currently 33 percent full and recent reports of low water clarity may impact trout fishing. Anglers are reminded to remove all vegetation from gear, boots and boats before leaving Hyatt. Last updated 11/23/26.

ILLINOIS RIVER: trout, steelhead

NO RECENT REPORTS 11/24/26.

LAKE SELMAC (Selmac Lake): trout, largemouth bass, bluegill, crappie

Bass and panfish are available, but one recent report said the aquatic vegetation is still a problem. Lake Selmac has its share of non-native aquatic hitchhikers. Boat anglers are asked to do their part to remove as much vegetation as possible before leaving the ramp, as well as drain and dry their vessel before boating in another waterbody. Last updated 11/24/2026.

LOST CREEK RESERVOIR: rainbow trout, landlocked spring chinook, bass

Lost Creek has dropped to 1,775 ft and is very low. The Takelma boat ramp is open. The Stewart/marina ramp is not available. The surface water temperature readings are unavailable, but likely near 50F. Trout can be caught at a variety of depths from the surface down to about 50 feet. Lures are often fished behind dodgers, and can be spiked with corn, worms or power worms. Lost Creek also offers good bank fishing access, and fishing on both sides of the dam can be very effective using PowerBait. Copepods are often present. The fish are safe to eat when cooked, and the copepods can be scraped off.

Anglers can get the latest reservoir details by calling the US Army Corps Lost Creek Lake and Applegate Reservoir projects information line at 1-800-472-2434. Last updated 11/24/26.

Rogue River, middle: hatchery coho, steelhead, trout

Flow in Grants Pass low and clear at 1,200cfs/1.11ft and the forecasted rain may bring the river up over the weekend. If the river comes up pulling plugs or plunking near the heads and tails of pools can be productive for hatchery Coho. Anglers, please use proper catch-and-release techniques, such as keeping fish in the water as much as possible and releasing them quickly. If fish are getting injured with the technique you are using, please change techniques. Remember that smaller rainbow are usually the steelhead that will return in future years. Current flow, temp and turbidity conditions for the Rogue can be found at the USGS stream gauges here, or checking the City of Grants Pass water page's river data here. Last updated 11/24/26.

Rogue River, upper: hatchery coho, steelhead, trout

Release out of Lost Cr is around 1,000cfs and the flow at Dodge Bridge is holding steady at 1120cfs/2.99ft, around 49F. It's low and clear, but some weather this weekend may cause coho to move upstream. Concentrating on the heads and tails of pools can be productive on the rise or with some rain. As of 11/24/26 the weekly Cole Rivers Hatchery trap counts are; coho 119 new, 412 season, summer steelhead 31 new, 481 season. Spring Chinook have spawned for the year, so please be mindful of where you wade to protect the eggs that are incubating. Anglers, please use proper catch-and-release techniques, such as keeping fish in the water as much as possible and releasing them quickly. If fish are getting injured with the technique you are using, please change techniques. Remember that smaller rainbow are usually the steelhead that will return in future years.

For up-to-date river levels, check all the USGS Rogue gauges here. Last updated 11/24/26.

Rogue River, above Lost Creek Reservoir: trout

The Rogue and tributaries above Lost Creek Reservoir remain open year-round, with a daily retention limit of 5 trout (no limit on brook trout). Area snow is patchy, but recent winds may be restricting some access points. Last updated 11/24/26.

WILLOW LAKE: rainbow trout, largemouth bass, black crappie, brown bullhead, yellow perch

The reservoir is very low but ice-free. The boat ramp is not usable, but bank angling near the dam may be an option for access. Last updated 11/24/26.

Willamette Zone -

  • Due to continuing dry conditions, Junction City Pond will not be stocked until the first week of December to allow for more rain to fill the pond.
  • Timber Linn in Albany, Walter Wirth Lake and Turner Lake in Salem are in good shape and have been stocked recently.

zones.name: Central Zone
zones.html:
Central Zone -

  • Following trophy trout stockings, the Fall River has been fishing exceptionally well.
  • Reports of consistent trout fishing on the lower Deschutes around the Trout Creek area.
  • Road closures and snow have limited access to many Central Zone lakes; however, lower elevation waterbodies including Lake Billy Chinook, Haystack Reservoir, and Ochoco Reservoir are good options during the winter months.

zones.name: Southeast Zone
zones.html:
SE Zone –

  • Fishing for trout at Lost Creek Reservoir.
  • Malheur Reservoir – great for Rainbow Trout from 10-22". Common sizes are 12-16" but we captured fish up to 22" in our sampling this week. We also fly-fished it in the evening and morning and had catches of 10+ trout/hr. We saw people having success trolling and bank fishing with bait as well. Water temperatures were in the mid 50's. You can launch a boat from the boat ramp. Water is up to the old school bus. If you know you know.
  • Yellowjacket Reservoir – Great fishing without a crowd! We sampled last week and found fish from 8-18" with a common size of 12-15". We fished leech patterns under an indicator midday and had non-stop action. Water temperatures are in the mid-50's here, too.
  • Lake of the Woods and Fourmile Lake were recently stocked with 12–14-inch rainbow trout.
  • Many streams are closed to protect spawning Redband Trout and Chinook Salmon in the Klamath Basin. Your best bets are Klamath Lake and Klamath River below Keno Dam for Redband Trout.
  • Yellow perch angling still might be good in Lake of the Woods, Gerber Reservoir and Upper Klamath Lake near Rocky Point.
  • Big Brown Trout are cruising the shoreline at Miller Lake. Snow might block access soon.
  • Crappie angling has been excellent at Dog Lake recently.

zones.name: Northeast Zone
zones.html:
NE Zone -

  • Tiger Muskies are hungry and aggressive at Phillips Reservoir. Try your luck before winter sets in. Water temperature is prime right now in the low 50°F. Fishing should remain hot until water temps drop below 45°F. As a bonus, the low water levels will concentrate fish and may make catching fish easier.
  • The Umatilla River should provide good coho fishing opportunity through the end of November. Steelhead are also disbursed throughout the river, but the highest concentrations are still in the lower portion.
  • Anglers are catching steelhead in both the Grande Ronde and Imnaha Rivers. Focus lower on both rivers this time of year. Fishing jigs under bobbers has been effective for catching late fall steelhead.

zones.name: Columbia River Zone
zones.html:
Columbia Fishing

November 25, 2026

Current and upcoming fishing opportunities:

Catch-and-release fishing for sturgeon is an option for anglers on the Columbia during the winter months.

Announcements

For the latest regulations, including in-season changes see the fishing regulation update page.

Printable 2026 Columbia River Recreational Fisheries Harvest Estimate Summary (pdf)

Fish consumption advisories

The Oregon Health Authority has issued consumption guidelines for parts of the Columbia River due to high levels of mercury and/or PCBs. Fish with these chemicals look, act, smell and taste like any other fish, so caution is important.

  • Bonneville Dam fish advisory
  • Safe fish choices for pregnancy and young children

Sign up for the latest information on boater access

Marine Board's Opportunities and Access Report incorporates information from federal and state agencies, local facility operators and fellow boaters to provide up-to-date information so boaters can decide where to recreate and what to expect this season. Subscribe to receive email updates.

Click here to find Columbia River regulation updates for salmon, steelhead, shad and sturgeon.

SALMON, STEELHEAD, AND SHAD

The lower Columbia creel program has ended for the year and will resume in February 2027. The creel program above Bonneville will continue for a couple more weeks.

Bonneville Dam to McNary Dam: Weekly checking showed four coho and for 11 boats (21 anglers).

STURGEON

Bonneville Dam to McNary Dam: No report.

WALLEYE

Bonneville Dam to McNary Dam: No report.

zones.name: Snake River Zone
zones.html:
Snake Zone –

  • Fall can be one of the best times of the year to fish for smallmouth and crappie as they stock up on forage for the winter. Look for these fish in shallow areas as they move closer to baitfish that are seeking warmer water temperatures near the surface of the reservoirs.
  • Updated changes to salmon and steelhead bag limits adjusted for Snake River started Sept 23. See the regulation updates page for more information.
  • Excess steelhead will be released into Hells Canyon Reservoir. Once they are released, they are considered trout and do not need to be recorded on a combined angling tag when harvested. See permanent regulations for details.

zones.name: Marine Zone
zones.html:
MARINE FISHING

November 25, 2026

As of Jan 1, 2026, an Ocean Endorsement is needed for most recreational anglers fishing in the ocean. Check the Ocean Endorsement page for more information.

Report unusual fish and ocean conditions

Have you encountered unusual fish or ocean conditions off the Oregon Coast this year? With warm El Niño waters pushing up the coast, we're starting to see unusual tropical visitors migrating north! Report your on-the-water observations to CaCurrent.Observations@noaa.gov (more information available here). Your observations are critical to understanding how changing ocean conditions affect what we see offshore.

Saltwater News Bulletins

Be among the first to know about in-season changes! You can subscribe to receive emails and text message alerts for marine topics that interest you. It's easy to unsubscribe at any time. Your contact information will remain confidential. Three different lists of interests to ocean enthusiasts are available: bottomfish, halibut and ocean salmon.

Bottomfish

A few reminders

  • Visit the sport bottomfish seasons page to see what's new for 2026.
  • Retention of quillback rockfish and yelloweye rockfish remains prohibited.
  • Cabezon is prohibited from Jan 1 through June 30.

Port by port reports for the week beginning Nov 16:

The weather system last week let up for one good day to fish.

Depoe Bay: Anglers who fished for rockfish landed near limits. Lingcod was excellent at 2.3 fish per angler.

Newport: Rockfish landings were just above 2.25 rockfish per angler. A mix of black, deacon, with a few cabezon and kelp greenling. Lingcod was slow at 0.65 fish per angler.

Brookings: Rockfish landings were around 2.5 fish per angler. Mainly black and deacon rockfishes with a few cabezon and kelp greenling. Lingcod was fair at 1 fish per angler.

The offshore long-leader fishery gives anglers an opportunity to catch more fish and to distribute effort away from nearshore species. Learn more about gear and the fishery.

Bottomfish fishing resources:

  • What can I keep and how many? Keep up with in-season regulation changes.
  • Know what you've caught with some helpful rockfish identification tips (including online quizzes and video).
  • Waypoints for fathom lines and other restricted areas.

Ocean salmon

Recreational ocean salmon fishing is now closed in all Oregon ocean areas. Season options for 2026 will be proposed in March.

Ocean salmon fishing resources:

  • Keep track of where salmon catch and quotas are at north of Cape Falcon and south of Cape Falcon
  • See the ocean salmon regulations in either a time and area graphic view or as a map

Pacific halibut

The Pacific halibut fishing season is now closed for the remainder of 2026. Season options for 2027 will be proposed in mid-February.

See Pacific halibut season dates or visit the sport halibut page for more information.

Shore and estuary fishing

Daily bag limits, seasons and licensing requirements for shore-based anglers are the same as for boat-based anglers.

There are plenty of rocky or sandy fishing sites up and down the coast where shore anglers can drop a line for saltwater fish. Read about how and where.

Lingcod and many other bottomfish species are available year-round to shore anglers fishing in rocky areas. A common setup for lingcod is a jig head with a rubber swim bait – it's simple but effective. Also pack a measuring device for lingcod: the minimum legal size is 22 inches.

Surfperch are available in the surf year-round along sandy beaches and rocky shores, with the best fishing (and safest fishing) occurring when swells are small. Find surfperch and other learn to fish workshops and events here.

Want more opportunities that don't include a boat? Check out the crabbing and clamming recreation report for updates on crabs, clams, mussels and more!

When fishing from shore or inside estuaries and bays, it is important to check the tide. Many fish that swim into estuaries and bays, including salmon, surfperch, and Pacific herring, tend to come in with the tide. Catch of these species is more likely to occur closer to slack tide. Additionally, the accessibility of some areas can be completely dependent on the tide. Do not allow the incoming tide to become a safety issue.
